chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man has wealth; should he purify it (pay zakat) if half a year has passed?' He said: 'No, but [he must wait] until a full year passes and it becomes due. Indeed, no one prays a prayer except at its appointed time, and similarly with zakat. And no one fasts the month of Ramadan except in its proper month, except for making up missed fasts. And every obligation is only fulfilled when it becomes due.'

key_terms.ٱلْحَوْلُ: A full lunar year (period for zakat)

ai.seo_question: When should zakat be paid on wealth? Is it permissible to pay it before the full year has passed?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the timing of zakat is strictly bound by the completion of the lunar year (hawl), rejecting early payment unless specifically permitted. He draws a parallel to the fixed times of prayer and fasting, emphasizing that all obligatory acts (fara'id) are only valid when their specific conditions and times are met. This underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of adhering to the precise temporal boundaries set by divine law for acts of worship.
